Subject: Priming samples & DB fallback plan for Apex onboarding

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we get Apex into sandbox, two parallel items we want to lock down this week so the implementation sprint is unblockable:

1) Priming / sample validation: we need a representative sample of user queries + ground-truth responses (200–500 rows) so our priming/priming-ablation runs and rerank evaluations are meaningful. I attached a tiny outline (priming_sample_outline.csv) with the fields we expect (query, user_metadata, ideal_response, doc_id, doc_text_snippet). If you can drop a small export to apex_small_sample.jsonl by EOD Thursday, we can get started.

2) Vector DB & fallback policy: during the demo you mentioned using a managed Pinecone instance. For production we recommend a two-tier strategy (primary: your Pinecone; fallback: Redwood-managed pgvector or a local Redis with vector plugin) with an automated traffic-shift policy for brief outages. I've cc'd Ben to sketch the fallback matrix.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm the export format for the sample (CSV vs JSONL)?
- Any regulatory constraints on storing embeddings outside your VPC?
- A 30–45 minute smoke-test window next week to try the fallback path (we can fail-over live with synthetic traffic).

Attachments: priming_sample_outline.csv

Best,
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Priming samples & DB fallback plan for Apex onboarding

Sarah —

Great, JSONL works. Quick notes on the fallback choices and expected tradeoffs:

Fallback options (short):
- Redwood-managed pgvector (Postgres): Pros = predictable cold-start, easier to snapshot and restore, transparent cost profile. Cons = slightly higher per-query latency for large vectors (we expect +25–35ms median on 1536-d vectors).
- RedisVector (self-managed or managed Redis with vector support): Pros = low latency for read-heavy traffic, good for small K. Cons = memory-heavy at scale; snapshotting is more involved.
- Remaining in Pinecone with a cross-region replica: Pros = minimal change to your stack; Cons = vendor dependency during outage windows.

Proposed fallback matrix (attached): in short, for initial go-live we recommend primary=Pinecone (customer-owned) + fallback=Redwood pgvector with automatic traffic shift after a 45s cumulative error threshold. We'll run a forced failover smoke test in a pre-prod window to measure the delta.

Ben (cc'd Karthik for ops/infra notes).

Attachments: db_fallback_matrix.xlsx

Regards,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Priming samples & DB fallback plan for Apex onboarding

Tom / Sarah —

We can do Tue 23 Nov 10:00–10:30 PST. Plan for the smoke test and rerank evaluation:

Smoke test steps (30m):
- 10:00–10:05: baseline traffic replay (record latencies & correctness)
- 10:05–10:12: force traffic to Redwood pgvector fallback for 7 minutes (monitor error rate, p50/p95 latency)
- 10:12–10:20: return to Pinecone; run a quick integrity check on top-K results
- 10:20–10:30: rerank evaluation run (we'll execute a 200-query job using the sample and generate a comparison report)

Rerank evaluation rubric:
- NDCG@10, MRR, precision@1 for top-5 candidates
- Thresholds for acceptance: NDCG delta <= 0.04 and precision@1 delta <= 0.03 vs baseline

Deliverables we will provide afterwards:
- CSV of per-query scores, p50/p95 latency table, and an audit log bundle (request_id, timestamp, route, input_hash).
- A short README with instructions to reproduce the runs.

Attached: rerank_eval_template.md for your review.

Grace O'Connor
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

- Fallback policy: primary=Pinecone (customer), fallback=Redwood pgvector; automatic traffic shift threshold = 45s cumulative error; logs will be zipped and handed to Apex within 2 hours of the test (Ben will prepare the audit bundle).

Open items:
- Legal/compliance signoff on transient embedding storage (Sarah to confirm by Mon 22 Nov).
- Confirm whether you need full document text for rerank (we recommend doc_snippet + doc_id to limit footprint).

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for Tue and a short pre-brief on Mon. Thanks again — excited to get Apex across the finish line.
